idea.description: Retrain the supplied corrected NextItNet with a strict ten-interaction causal context at every supervised output position. Independently encode overlapping raw-item windows using the same jointly trained backbone and item embeddings, scoring only each window's terminal feature. Preserve all inherited targets, negatives, objective and optimizer initially. This remains one network and one selected checkpoint per category. Treat W=10 as a predeclared experimental control rather than an established optimal horizon.
idea.motivation: The experiment explicitly targets two user-facing failures: older isolated interests displacing recent-purpose recommendations, and broadly associated historical interests displacing more specific current matches. Restricting raw inputs directly removes distant evidence from each prediction; it does not ensure that retained recent evidence expresses current intent. The model-facing hypothesis is that contextual interference contributes to Electronics' measured 6.84% sampled training negative-beats-positive rate and 0.4512 lower-decile margin. That connection remains unproven: permutation sensitivity establishes order dependence, and sparse matched replacement support cannot establish stale-history harm. At 20% progress, a retrained context restriction is a useful controlled experiment before adding more gates or mining. Uniform multi-negative CE remains a simpler alternative if window computation proves unaffordable. The supplied inspiration scores are descriptive search results, not evidence that architectural differences caused their ordering. Correct the earlier shortcut argument: identity shortcuts preserve already encoded information but do not move information across time, guarantee distant-history retention, or prevent learned suppression and cancellation.
idea.implementation_notes:
Apply the change within the host-supplied corrected baseline; its source and complete inherited configuration were not included here, so do not invent a replacement scaffold or standalone train.py. Fix W=10 before training. Record the inherited causal residual-convolution implementation, hidden width, every kernel and dilation, normalization, embedding initialization, positional dependence, dropout, scoring head, objective reduction, optimizer, clipping, sample_batch behavior, negative exclusions and checkpoint cadence. Retain these settings initially. Do not introduce experimental gates into the corrected cold start. No code execution, diagnostics or training has occurred in this report.

For every inherited valid aligned target at position t, construct its chronologically ordered suffix ending at input position t and containing at most ten nonpadding raw item IDs. The aligned positive remains the next-item target and must not be included in its own input window. Use the sampler's existing context boundary; do not silently recover earlier interactions outside that boundary. Preserve exactly the original valid targets and negative IDs. Merely truncating each original sequence to its final ten positions would discard supervised targets and introduce another experimental change.

Left-pad windows to length ten when the inherited backbone supports variable lengths without changing absolute-position or boundary conventions. Corrected position-free NextItNet can ordinarily use this construction, but verify the actual supplied implementation. If absolute positions or fixed-shape operations exist, preserve original position IDs or left-pad to the inherited length as required; document the selected behavior and its extra cost before training. Do not claim equivalence between the alternatives without checking it. Apply identical window length, raw-input construction, positional rules and padding masks in training, diagnostics and prediction. Ten interactions do not represent a fixed elapsed-time horizon.

Run every window through the same corrected backbone and gather its largest nonpadding positional index. Scatter terminal features back into B x L x D for the public log2feats(sequence) interface, returning zeros at padded input positions. Window extraction must start from raw item IDs and embeddings: slicing contextualized full-history states retains older dependencies. All windows share every model parameter, and their predictions are never averaged or fused. The strict bound follows from computational exclusion of older inputs, provided no persistent state, cross-window normalization or other cross-example communication exists. It does not imply equivalence to an ordinary full-sequence pass inside the window; padding boundaries and realized dropout differ.

Preserve zero padding embeddings and the corrected baseline's masking after operations that can generate nonzero padded states, including biased convolutions, affine normalization and residual updates. Use tokenwise normalization over channels, preserving the baseline implementation. If the supplied model instead uses cross-example normalization, flag that incompatibility before execution rather than silently altering the architecture. Causal convolutions, gate inputs if inherited, and every bypass must operate only on the extracted window. Structural receptive-field span is R=1+sum_l((k_l-1)*d_l), counting every temporal convolution within every residual block. Possible offsets can have gaps, and span is not effective learned influence. The explicit raw-input restriction bounds accessible history regardless of a larger backbone receptive field.

Training should lazily enumerate valid target windows and microbatch windows directly, including when a single original example has many targets. Avoid constructing a full B x L x inherited_length tensor or retaining graph-connected features for all targets before backward. For an original logical batch containing N valid targets, zero gradients once. For each window microbatch, compute the inherited per-target loss, sum it, divide by N, and backward immediately; retain weights throughout accumulation, clip once and step once afterward. This specifies a position-mean objective. Confirm the inherited baseline uses the same reduction; if it does not, reproduce its exact target weights in both conditions and disclose the difference rather than silently changing reduction. An empty logical batch follows the inherited skip behavior and is counted. Internal windows and microbatches are components of one logical batch, not extra training batches.

Use the public bounded log2feats interface for compatibility; use a shared terminal-window encoding helper directly in training so that memory-bounded backward does not require materializing all B x L graph-connected features. Both routes must call identical backbone code. With AMP, retain one scale throughout accumulation, unscale once after all microbatches, then clip and step according to PyTorch guidance. Do not divide uneven microbatch means equally. Chunked and unchunked deterministic gradients should agree within numerical tolerance when dropout is disabled and normalization is sample-independent. Dropout generally changes realized masks under windowing and microbatching; independent masks preserve the expected additive loss but alter gradient correlations relative to shared sequence activations. Do not claim exact stochastic equivalence without replaying masks.

Compute is a material risk. With N approximately B*L supervised positions, independent length-ten windows require roughly ten times the temporal convolution work of ordinary B x L encoding, before launch overhead and lost activation reuse; padding each window to the inherited length can be substantially worse. Backbone work scales approximately as O(N*W*D*K*H^2), with microbatch activation memory O(m*W*D*H), excluding parameters, optimizer state and output scoring. Lazy extraction and microbatching reduce memory, not repeated computation. Measure the host-accounted runtime of a short implementation check before committing a long run. Choose and record a fixed microbatch size that fits, rather than promising a trial count without timing evidence. If infeasible within the remaining budget, retain the proposal as untested and prioritize the uniform-negative objective experiment; do not silently change epochs, batches or target coverage.

Compare the independently trained full-context corrected control with recent-ten context using identical targets, negative IDs, original batch ordering, capacity, optimizer updates, seed and inherited checkpoint schedule. Use a dedicated reproducible stream or recorded inherited draws where needed to prevent windowing-related dropout RNG consumption from changing future target/negative sampling. Use stable category identifiers rather than process-randomized Python hashes. Match shared initial parameters and record any unavoidable stochastic differences. Do not access other trials or reuse their trained checkpoints. Controls are separate experiments whose outputs are never combined.

If budget permits, predeclare two explanatory controls. First, select at most ten chronologically ordered, history-spanning items from the same available prefix: for n>10 take indices floor(j*(n-1)/9) for j=0,...,9; for n<=10 retain all items. This includes the terminal item, has unique indices when n>10, and matches the recent-ten input count. Second, test a separately declared full-context regularization configuration, logging its changed dropout or regularization coefficient. These controls can help distinguish recency concentration from information budget and regularization, but cannot identify user intent or fully isolate optimization effects. Keep their number small and count every attempt against the budget. Inspect existing convergence logs and losses without introducing an expanded checkpoint search. Equal update counts do not imply equal compute, gradient noise or optimization trajectories.

Use identical bounded encoding in ModelView and inference. Preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), the host ModelView interfaces and view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. The generated working/predict.py must embed the same shared architecture, terminal-window helper, positional configuration, masking and checkpoint format. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Preserve fixed diagnostic negatives and margin definitions for comparability. Before long training, verify aligned target preservation and absence of target leakage, causal behavior under future-input perturbation, invariance to every raw item outside the ten-interaction window, left-padding and all-padding handling, and generated-predictor score agreement. Verify terminal-only inference against bounded log2feats, and chunked versus unchunked gradients on a tiny deterministic batch with dropout disabled. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 logical batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and inherited validation/checkpoint cadence. Respect the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200 despite its family-agnostic name. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl with unchanged routing. Preserve its tie handling. Fixed-candidate sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog performance. Where the host exposes paired user-hit indicators and permitted history descriptors, report gained/lost hits and exploratory differences by available history length and the elapsed span of the last ten observed events. Analyze last-observed-event-to-target gaps only if validation timestamps are already available through an authorized host interface; otherwise mark this analysis unavailable rather than obtaining extra labels or files. Predeclare strata and disclose small counts.

If paired indicators are available, use descriptive category-stratified paired bootstrap intervals: resample users within each category with matching indices across variants, calculate category differences, then average them equally. A reproducible analysis can use 10,000 replicates and analysis seed 42. If users overlap across routes, use an appropriate user-cluster procedure preserving equal category weighting or disclose the independence assumption. Intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates, omit training-seed and candidate-redraw variation, and do not correct repeated validation selection. Record all attempted configurations and regard searched gains as exploratory.

Overfitting and shortcuts remain possible. A short window can regularize capacity use or amplify recent-item memorization, popularity associations and last-item shortcuts without improving current-need reasoning. Inference-only terminal-preserving permutations or terminal-item interventions on the same trained network can describe dependence, but introduce distribution shift and do not establish causal preferences. Compare convergence and available training-frequency strata descriptively without fitting an auxiliary recommendation scorer. A validation gain establishes usefulness under this protocol; attributing it specifically to stale-interest removal requires supporting controls and qualitative evidence.

Use only the prescribed twenty real training users, five per category, for full-catalog unseen-item qualitative follow-up. Track older-interest displacement and broad-association displacement separately, alongside concrete current matches, duplicate-function rejection, unsupported compatibility, excessive quantity, unestablished projects and uncertain identity. Missing identity evidence is distinct from explicit dislike. Only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions are available; ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable despite generic upstream schemas. Bounded context cannot establish compatibility, replacement need or unmet demand, and may discard useful persistent preferences. No behavioral gain follows solely from larger training margins.

References supporting implementation and interpretation include NextItNet and its authors' repository for causal architecture and sequence-length comparison cautions; Understanding the Effective Receptive Field in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for possible versus effective influence; and PyTorch AMP examples for gradient accumulation. Highway Networks, WaveNet and ReZero constrain gating novelty claims. MARS motivates attribute specificity but uses pretrained language models, so it does not validate the proposed scratch text alternative. The supplied adjacent sequence-length and time-aware augmentation evidence does not establish an optimal ten-event NextItNet horizon on these four categories.
idea.pseudocode:
CONTEXT_WINDOW = 10
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']

# Integrate into the supplied corrected NextItNet; preserve its shared backbone.
# All helpers use only the context already supplied by the inherited sampler.
def raw_windows(sequence, target_positions):
    for b, t in target_positions:
        ids = nonpadding_ids(sequence[b, :t + 1])[-CONTEXT_WINDOW:]
        yield left_pad_with_recorded_baseline_conventions(ids), (b, t)

class BoundedNextItNet:
    # item_emb and corrected_backbone belong to this one trained network.
    def encode_window_terminal(self, windows):
        features = self.corrected_backbone(windows)
        last = maximum_nonpadding_position(windows)  # never count-1
        return gather_with_inherited_empty_history_handling(features, last)

    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        # Public B x L x D compatibility path; training uses helper directly.
        positions = nonpadding_positions(sequence)
        values = self.encode_window_terminal(raw_windows(sequence, positions))
        return differentiable_scatter_into_zero_B_L_D(values, positions)

for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    sampler = inherited_sampler_with_reproducible_independent_rng(...)
    model = BoundedNextItNet(inherited_config)
    for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            batch = sampler.sample_batch(...)  # preserve targets and negatives
            valid = inherited_valid_target_mask(batch)
            N = int(valid.sum())
            if N == 0:
                record_inherited_empty_batch_behavior()
                continue
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            # Lazy target-window chunks bound memory even for long examples.
            for positions in fixed_microbatches(valid_positions(valid)):
                windows = raw_windows(batch.sequence, positions)
                features = model.encode_window_terminal(windows)
                losses = inherited_target_losses(
                    model, features, batch.positive[positions],
                    batch.negative[positions])
                loss = losses.sum() / N  # confirm inherited position-mean reduction
                backward_with_inherited_precision_policy(loss)
            unscale_once_if_using_amp()
            inherited_clipping_if_present()
            optimizer_step_once_with_inherited_precision_policy()
        inherited_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(
        category, context_window=10,
        window_policy=recorded_padding_and_position_policy,
        architecture=inherited_config)

write_predictor_using_identical_architecture_and_terminal_window_helper()

Use capacity-correct bipartite matching as a necessary feasibility check and search bound, then explicitly enforce joint sequence and cross-plan constraints. Separate construction recovery from the assignment selector and its sensitivity estimand; fit no additional predictor.
idea_diagnosis.motivation: Displayed dose-one replacement effects in Movies and Electronics each involve only one retained user; the supplied Industrial and CDs summaries expose permutation results without successful replacement blocks. These summaries motivate investigating construction failure, but omitted entries must not be treated as proof of exhaustive failure. Existing definitions explicitly acknowledge that greedy failure does not establish infeasibility. Exact feasibility auditing addresses this measurement limitation before replacement sensitivity motivates training changes. It cannot guarantee additional supported users or better validation HR@10. Minimum-distance selection also changes the intervention mechanism, so its effects cannot automatically be interpreted as a more accurate estimate of the original randomized replacement effect.

Preregister the existing users, cuts, doses, lag bins, replacement repetitions, candidate-generation rules, frequency matching, reachability matching, transition constraints and reuse rules. Retain the existing deterministic prefix selection and sample caps rather than selecting additional cases after seeing effects. Freeze replacement positions, doses, candidate pools, admissibility edges and whole-block predicates before either constructor runs. Do not relax constraints or expand pools in response to solver failure or model scores. Hash and serialize each finite pool, ordered domains, constraints and protocol version. Feasibility conclusions apply to those finite pools, not every catalog item. Where temporal availability cannot be established from available timestamps, report the limitation rather than asserting historical availability. Training transition counts define diagnostic plausibility only; they do not establish behavioral relevance or supply recommendation scores.

For each jointly required recent/older and random/constrained four-plan block, represent intervention positions as slots and admissible replacement IDs as edges. Item capacity and uniqueness must follow the existing protocol: allow cross-plan reuse when permitted, and enforce shared capacity only when explicitly required. Ordinary maximum bipartite matching certifies the corresponding slotwise all-different problem, not arbitrary additional constraints. Use a capacity flow or correctly scoped item copies when appropriate; constraints spanning overlapping reuse groups remain explicit search predicates. Record isolated slots and independently checkable deficiency certificates when available. For unit-capacity graphs, a Hall witness consists of a slot subset whose neighbor set is smaller than that subset. A covering matching does not establish whole-block feasibility.

Use deterministic depth-first branch-and-bound for the small number of replacement slots. Order slots by remaining admissible count, breaking ties by serialized slot ID. Order candidates by a preregistered training-only distance and item ID. Validate capacity, partial predicates and joint constraints as soon as they become decidable, then run an independent complete-assignment checker before accepting any solution. A matching bound on remaining domains can reject branches unable to complete. Do not prune an edge because one maximum matching omitted it. If domain filtering is added, use Régin-style supported-edge filtering or the simpler correctness reference: force the edge and test whether the remaining variables admit a covering matching. Additional joint predicates can invalidate assignments even when every edge passes this necessary test.

Separate two modes. The primary feasibility audit seeks any valid complete block and can stop at the first one; it does not claim minimum distance. An optional selector study minimizes a fixed additive replacement distance among complete valid assignments. Preserve existing protocol distances where possible. If distance uses embeddings, freeze the trained model and identify the selector as model-dependent. Smaller distance need not imply a smaller model response. Initialize optimization with the original greedy assignment only after independent validation; retain that exact assignment for the legacy diagnostic whenever it is valid. With a feasible incumbent of cost U, prune an improvement branch only when a valid lower bound is at least U. A minimum-cost assignment on a relaxation that drops joint predicates supplies a lower bound when its capacity semantics are correct; a simple sum of remaining slot minima is another valid, possibly weaker bound. An arbitrary objective cutoff is not a feasible incumbent. Exhausting an improvement search proves the incumbent optimal, not the original problem infeasible. If lexicographic tie optimality is claimed, continue or constrain search appropriately; otherwise document deterministic first-found handling of equal-cost solutions.

Propose a fixed cap of 10,000 expanded search nodes per block and an aggregate synchronized diagnostic safety cap of 30 seconds per category; these are proposed limits, not measured costs. Define a node as one entered partial-assignment state, including the root, and record matching calls, candidate checks, pool-building work and elapsed time separately. Use single-threaded search, fixed software versions, seed, parameters, domain order and matching implementation. Deterministic node limits improve repeatability but do not equalize computational effort. The wall-time safety cap can change completed work across machines; mark this explicitly. Preserve feasible incumbents at any interruption. Mark unstarted blocks after the aggregate cap as unresolved, never silently exclude them.

Return separate feasibility and optimization fields. Feasibility is certified_feasible after independent checking, certified_infeasible after a sound certificate or exhaustive unpruned feasibility search, or unresolved otherwise. Optimization status is not_requested, feasible_unproven or proven_optimal, with incumbent cost, valid lower bound and gap where available. Time- or node-limited search without an incumbent remains unresolved. A complete feasible incumbent may be scored even when its optimality is unproven. Greedy success with an invalid or missing retained incumbent is an implementation warning, not evidence of infeasibility. Flag conflicting certificates or numerical inconsistencies as errors and exclude affected effects with explicit reasons.

Validate the solver independently before real probes using tiny exhaustive instances and a separate direct constraint checker. Compare feasible sets, optimum values and status classifications. Include surplus candidate values, empty domains, Hall violations without isolated slots, valid covering matchings defeated by pairwise constraints, permitted cross-plan reuse, shared capacities, tied costs, feasible greedy incumbents and interrupted searches before and after finding an incumbent. Check that every pruning rule preserves all truly feasible assignments and that interruption never erases a validated incumbent. Exhaustive tiny tests provide implementation evidence, not a proof for arbitrary code.

Fixed admissibility defines F(h), not a probability distribution over assignments. Explicitly identify the original constructor's law, including seed derivation, candidate order, retries, rejection, failure and repeated-draw rules; do not call it uniform unless established. For randomized selectors, sensitivity is S(q) = E_h E_{a drawn from q(.|h)}[delta(h,a)], conditional on the stated population and completion rules. A deterministic first-feasible or minimum-distance selector defines a different, point-mass intervention. Random edge costs followed by matching do not imply uniform matching samples. Independent RNG repetitions reproduce the implemented law, not an unspecified target law. Do not importance-weight deterministic optimizer outputs to recover an unrestricted random-assignment average. Approximate uniform sampling would require a separate justified algorithm and error characterization and is outside this minimal experiment.

Run greedy and exact construction on identical frozen pools and planned seeds. Report completion separately from sensitivity. Preserve valid legacy assignments rather than replacing them merely because a lower-distance assignment exists. For rescued blocks, report sensitivity under the documented recovery selector as a separate estimand. An optional selector comparison uses common certified-feasible histories, identical positions and counts; report incomplete selector runs rather than conditioning silently on their success. Prespecified distance bands, position-specific distances and candidate characteristics help describe selector differences but do not equate assignment laws or identify causal intent. Repeated assignments per history, if budgeted, characterize assignment variation under each actual law; deterministic selectors have no within-history random-assignment variation.

Separate graph deficiency, exhaustive joint infeasibility, feasible construction, unresolved search and implementation errors. Report eligible users, users with certified-feasible blocks, retained blocks, rescued blocks and support by history length and training frequency. Count each distinct planned block once. If F blocks are certified feasible, I certified infeasible and U unresolved among N = F + I + U error-free planned blocks, eventual feasibility is bounded by [F/N, (F+U)/N]. Report implementation errors separately and provide a conservative bound including them as unknown if a bound over all planned blocks is needed. These are identification bounds conditional on fixed pools, not sampling confidence intervals. For user-level feasibility defined as at least one feasible block, derive bounds from each user's block statuses instead of reusing block fractions. Report cap hits and elapsed times as censored work-to-completion observations; do not substitute a cutoff for a completed runtime or average only completed runs as an unrestricted runtime estimate.

Report effects separately on common successful support and exact-only support; their union changes the supported population. On common support, distinguish changing the assignment selector from changing the constructor. Do not attribute changed averages solely to better estimation or apply unsupported selection weights. Multiple planned corruption draws do not add users. Retain full raw assignments, IDs, positions, distances, seeds, solver statuses, failures and counts so support-specific summaries can be recomputed.

Keep in-place edits, unchanged terminal item, occupied positions, left padding and timestamps. Gather the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1; exclude empty histories. Inputs contain training-prefix interactions only, without the target occurrence or subsequent sequence context. Preserve fixed original-full-prefix eligibility, target retained once, PAD exclusion, repeated-target flags, shared restricted catalogs, inserted-item decomposition, exact chunked ranks with ascending-ID ties, and existing identity/causality/padding controls. Structural reachability remains an accessibility control, not evidence of useful learned influence. Encode each unique history once, stream catalog scores and validate rank counting against exhaustive synthetic sorting.

Average prescribed assignment repetitions within prefixes and prefixes within users. Resample whole users within categories, retaining every selected user's prefixes, perturbations, solver statuses and paired method results; recompute support-specific statistics in each replicate. Keep assignment Monte Carlo summaries separate from between-user uncertainty. Intervals remain exploratory and fragile with few clusters; return them unavailable below two supported users, and flag bootstrap replicates with undefined support. Compute an equal-weight four-category macro only when all four categories have defined measurements; do not pool users across categories or replace missing categories. Preserve RNG states and individual module modes in finally, using a diagnostic RNG independent of training.

Return measured metrics, metric_definitions, protocol, raw assignment records, support denominators, unavailable reasons, solver bounds and synchronized cost. The interpretation prompt must distinguish construction feasibility, selection mechanism, conditional sensitivity, identification bounds and sampling uncertainty. All computation counts against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; the host remains authoritative for accounting. Freeze constraints, distances and selectors before observing their score effects to reduce diagnostic overfitting. Repeatedly selecting protocols from training-prefix sensitivity can favor memorized transitions, popularity-matched candidates or unusually easy supported users. Monitor these strata without asserting causal preferences. def raw_windows(sequence, target_positions):

class BoundedNextItNet:
    # item_emb and corrected_backbone belong to this one trained network.
    def encode_window_terminal(self, windows):
        features = self.corrected_backbone(windows)
        last = maximum_nonpadding_position(windows)  # never count-1
        return gather_with_inherited_empty_history_handling(features, last)

    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        # Public B x L x D compatibility path; training uses helper directly.
        positions = nonpadding_positions(sequence)
        values = self.encode_window_terminal(raw_windows(sequence, positions))
        return differentiable_scatter_into_zero_B_L_D(values, positions)

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = capture_module_modes_and_rng_states(self.view.model)
        try:
            rng = dedicated_generator(seed=42)
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                protocol = frozen_protocol()
                baseline_metrics = existing_family_aware_probes(train_loader)
                prefixes = fixed_training_prefix_sample(self.view.user_train, protocol)
                pools = training_only_frequency_and_local_neighborhoods(self.view)
                architecture = inspect_actual_temporal_dependencies(self.view.model)
                records = []
                for category, user, sequence, target in prefixes:
                    if not sequence.ne(0).any():
                        record_skip('all_padding')
                        continue
                    candidates = frozen_original_prefix_eligibility(sequence, target)
                    clean = measure(self.view, sequence, target, candidates,
                                    readout='maximum_nonpadding_index',
                                    rank='chunked_score_then_item_id')
                    bands = matched_lag_positions(sequence, architecture,
                                                  keep_terminal=True)
                    for dose, draw, replacement_type in protocol.conditions:
                        plans = paired_replacement_plans(
                            sequence, target, bands, pools, rng,
                            dose=dose, replacement_type=replacement_type)
                        for plan in plans:
                            if not plan.matches_protocol:
                                record_matching_failure(plan)
                                continue
                            altered = replace_items_in_place(sequence, plan)
                            changed = measure(self.view, altered, target, candidates)
                            inserted = set(plan.replacement_ids)
                            restricted = candidates.without(inserted)
                            clean_restricted = measure(self.view, sequence, target, restricted)
                            changed_restricted = measure(self.view, altered, target, restricted)
                            records.append(paired_record(
                                category, user, clean, changed,
                                clean_restricted, changed_restricted,
                                inserted_item_effects=True, matching=plan.metadata))
                controls = identity_causality_chunking_and_applicable_reachability_checks()
                metrics = aggregate_within_user_then_bootstrap_within_category(records)
                metrics.update(separate_corruption_monte_carlo_error(records))
                metrics.update(baseline_metrics)
                return {'metrics': attach_protocol_coverage_controls_and_cost(metrics, controls),
                        'metric_definitions': definitions_with_estimands_counts_and_limitations()}
        finally:
            restore_module_modes_and_rng_states(saved)

    itemnum = 0

    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    batch_size: int,
    maxlen: int,
    *,
    num_negatives: int = 1,
):
    if min(itemnum, batch_size, maxlen, num_negatives) < 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "itemnum, batch_size, maxlen and num_negatives must be positive"
        )
    users = [u for u, items in user_train.items() if len(items) >= 2]
    if not users:
        raise RuntimeError("no users with at least two training interactions")
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg = [], [], []
    catalog = range(1, itemnum + 1)
    for _ in range(batch_size):
        history = user_train[random.choice(users)]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        neg = np.zeros((maxlen, num_negatives), dtype=np.int64)
        start = max(0, len(history) - 1 - maxlen)
        offset = maxlen - (len(history) - 1 - start)
        # Retain observations preceding the truncated input window, but never
        # exclude later interactions or held-out labels.
        prefix = {value for value in history[:start] if 1 <= value <= itemnum}
        for index in range(start, len(history) - 1):
            position = offset + index - start
            item, target = history[index], history[index + 1]
            if not (1 <= item <= itemnum and 1 <= target <= itemnum):
                raise ValueError("Training interaction outside the item vocabulary")
            seq[position] = item
            pos[position] = target
            prefix.add(item)
            available = itemnum - len(prefix) - int(target not in prefix)
            count = min(num_negatives, available)
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            if available <= max(4 * count, itemnum // 4):
                # Dense exclusions: sample the explicit eligible catalog.
                eligible = [
                    value
                    for value in catalog
                    if value not in prefix and value != target
                ]
                chosen = random.sample(eligible, count)
            else:
                # Sparse exclusions: rejection sampling avoids drawing an
                # extra candidate for every historical item. Accepted IDs are
                # an ordered uniform sample without replacement.
                chosen = []
                selected = set()
                attempts = 0
                while len(chosen) < count and attempts < 8 * count:
                    value = random.randint(1, itemnum)
                    attempts += 1
                    if (
                        value not in prefix
                        and value != target
                        and value not in selected
                    ):
                        selected.add(value)
                        chosen.append(value)
                if len(chosen) < count:
                    eligible = [
                        value
                        for value in catalog
                        if value not in prefix
                        and value != target
                        and value not in selected
                    ]
                    chosen.extend(random.sample(eligible, count - len(chosen)))
            neg[position, :count] = chosen
        batch_seq.append(seq)
        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg[:, 0] if num_negatives == 1 else neg)
    # Default diagnostic calls retain B x L; only training requests B x L x K.
    return np.asarray(batch_seq), np.asarray(batch_pos), np.asarray(batch_neg)

) -> torch.Tensor:

    seq: torch.Tensor,
    pos: torch.Tensor,
    neg: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    target_positions: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    reduction: str = "mean",

    def __init__(
        self, hidden_units: int, dilation: int, kernel_size: int, dropout_rate: float

        self.kernel_size = kernel_size

    def _causal_conv(self, conv: nn.Conv1d, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        dilation = conv.dilation[0]
        kernel = conv.kernel_size[0]
        active_taps = min(kernel, 1 + (x.size(-1) - 1) // dilation)
        pad = (active_taps - 1) * dilation
        padded = nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, 0))
        # Conv1d stores the current-position tap last. Earlier omitted taps
        # multiply only zeros and have zero gradient in the original operation.
        if active_taps == kernel:
            return conv(padded)
        return nn.functional.conv1d(
            padded,
            conv.weight[..., kernel - active_taps :].contiguous(),
            conv.bias,
            stride=conv.stride,
            dilation=conv.dilation,
            groups=conv.groups,
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        residual = x
        y = (self.norm1(x) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._causal_conv(self.conv1, y).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self.dropout(self.activation(y))
        y = (self.norm2(y) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._causal_conv(self.conv2, y).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self.dropout(y)
        return (residual + y) * mask

            raise ValueError("Expected B x L histories with 0 < L <= maxlen")

            min(self.context_window, sequence.size(1)), dim=1, sorted=True

        # Keep those IDs instead of renumbering each independently encoded window.

    def predict_score(
        self, features: torch.Tensor, items: torch.Tensor

        embeddings = self.item_emb(items)
        if features.shape[:-1] == items.shape:
            return (features * embeddings).sum(dim=-1)
        if items.ndim == features.ndim and items.shape[:-1] == features.shape[:-1]:

        return scores.detach().double().cpu().numpy()

    def _catalog_scores(self, history, ids, chunk):
        # Only one feature computation and chunk-bounded GPU scoring per history.
        ids = np.asarray(ids, dtype=np.int64)
        if (
            chunk < 1
            or ids.ndim != 1
            or len(ids) == 0
            or np.any(ids < 1)
            or np.any(ids > int(self.network.itemnum))
            or np.any(ids[1:] <= ids[:-1])
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Expected positive chunk size and sorted unique in-catalog IDs"
            )
        feature = self._feature(history)
        scores = np.empty(len(ids), dtype=np.float64)
        for start in range(0, len(ids), chunk):
            scores[start : start + chunk] = self._scores(
                feature, ids[start : start + chunk]
            )
        return scores

    def _result(self, ids, scores, target, sampled, removed=(), include_top10=True):
        ids = np.asarray(ids, dtype=np.int64)
        scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
        if (
            ids.ndim != 1
            or scores.shape != ids.shape
            or len(ids) == 0
            or np.any(ids < 1)
            or np.any(ids > int(self.network.itemnum))
            or np.any(ids[1:] <= ids[:-1])
            or not np.isfinite(scores).all()
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid sorted catalog IDs or aligned finite scores")
        removed = set(removed)
        keep = ~np.isin(ids, list(removed)) if removed else slice(None)
        catalog, values = ids[keep], scores[keep]
        index = int(np.searchsorted(catalog, target))
        if index == len(catalog) or int(catalog[index]) != target:
            raise ValueError("Target missing from diagnostic catalog")
        score = float(values[index])
        rank = 1
        top_ids, top_scores = np.empty(0, dtype=np.int64), np.empty(0)
        for start in range(0, len(catalog), 4096):
            chunk_ids = catalog[start : start + 4096]
            chunk_scores = values[start : start + 4096]
            rank += int(self._ahead(chunk_scores, chunk_ids, score, target).sum())
            if include_top10:
                # Retain each chunk's top ten, including ascending-ID tie order.
                # Every global top-ten item must be in its own chunk's top ten.
                order = np.lexsort((chunk_ids, -chunk_scores))[:10]
                top_ids = np.concatenate((top_ids, chunk_ids[order]))
                top_scores = np.concatenate((top_scores, chunk_scores[order]))
                order = np.lexsort((top_ids, -top_scores))[:10]
                top_ids, top_scores = top_ids[order], top_scores[order]
        negatives = np.asarray([i for i in sampled if i not in removed], dtype=np.int64)
        if (
            negatives.ndim != 1
            or len(np.unique(negatives)) != len(negatives)
            or np.any(negatives == target)
            or not np.isin(negatives, catalog).all()
        ):
            raise ValueError("Sampled negatives must be unique eligible non-target IDs")
        margin = None
        if len(negatives):
            margin = float(score - values[np.searchsorted(catalog, negatives)].mean())
        return {
            "rank": rank,
            "hr10": float(rank <= 10),
            "score": score,
            "margin": margin,
            "top10": top_ids.tolist() if include_top10 else None,
            "catalog_size": len(catalog),
            "margin_negatives": len(negatives),
        }

    def _architecture(self, history):
        import inspect

        # Verify the supplied forward implementations before using their graph.
        # Otherwise numerical controls remain available, but reachability is unknown.
        offsets, convs, reason = {0}, [], None
        try:
            encode = inspect.getsource(type(self.network)._encode_raw_windows)
            windows = inspect.getsource(type(self.network).raw_windows)
            terminal = inspect.getsource(type(self.network).encode_window_terminal)
            block_code = [
                inspect.getsource(type(b).forward) for b in self.network.blocks
            ]
            known = (
                type(self.network).__name__ == "NextItNetModel"
                and self.network.context_window == 10
                and "self.pos_emb(position_ids)" in encode
                and "x = block(x, mask)" in encode
                and "return self.norm(x) * mask" in encode
                and "indices[None, :] <= terminal[:, None]" in windows
                and "min(self.context_window, sequence.size(1))" in windows
                and "self._encode_raw_windows(windows, position_ids)" in terminal
                and all(
                    "return (residual + y) * mask" in s
                    and "self.norm1(x) * mask" in s
                    and "self.norm2(y) * mask" in s
                    for s in block_code
                )
                and all(
                    isinstance(b.norm1, torch.nn.LayerNorm)
                    and isinstance(b.norm2, torch.nn.LayerNorm)
                    and tuple(b.norm1.normalized_shape) == (self.network.hidden_units,)
                    and tuple(b.norm2.normalized_shape) == (self.network.hidden_units,)
                    for b in self.network.blocks
                )
            )
            if not known:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Forward implementation differs from supplied raw-window NextItNet"
                )
            for block in self.network.blocks:
                branch = set(offsets)
                for conv in (block.conv1, block.conv2):
                    if (
                        not isinstance(conv, torch.nn.Conv1d)
                        or conv.stride != (1,)
                        or conv.padding != (0,)
                    ):
                        raise ValueError("Unsupported convolution geometry")
                    if conv.dilation != (block.dilation,) or conv.kernel_size != (
                        block.kernel_size,
                    ):
                        raise ValueError(
                            "Causal padding and convolution attributes differ"
                        )
                    taps = {i * conv.dilation[0] for i in range(conv.kernel_size[0])}
                    branch = {a + b for a in branch for b in taps}
                    convs.append(
                        {"kernel": conv.kernel_size[0], "dilation": conv.dilation[0]}
                    )
                offsets |= branch
            # Probe histories are contiguous nonpadding items. Independently
            # encoded raw windows exclude all earlier items before convolution.
            # This positional interpretation does not extend to inputs with gaps.
            offsets &= set(range(int(self.network.context_window)))
        except (AttributeError, TypeError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            offsets, reason = None, str(exc)
        seq = self._pack(history)
        features = self.model.log2feats(seq)
        pivot = seq.size(1) - len(history) + (len(history) - 1) // 2
        changed = seq.clone()
        suffix = changed[:, pivot + 1 :]
        changed[:, pivot + 1 :] = 1 + suffix.remainder(int(self.network.itemnum))
        count = int((seq != changed).sum())
        altered = self.model.log2feats(changed)
        causal_error = float(
            (features[:, : pivot + 1] - altered[:, : pivot + 1]).abs().max()
        )
        empty_norm = float(
            self.model.log2feats(torch.zeros_like(seq)).norm(dim=-1).max()
        )
        unreachable = next(
            (
                i
                for i in range(len(history) - 1)
                if offsets is not None and len(history) - 1 - i not in offsets
            ),
            None,
        )
        unreachable_error = None
        if unreachable is not None and int(self.network.itemnum) > 1:
            control = list(history)
            control[unreachable] = 1 + control[unreachable] % int(self.network.itemnum)
            unreachable_error = float(
                (self._feature(control) - features[0, -1]).abs().max()
            )
        return {
            "convolutions": convs,
            "structural_possible_offsets": (
                sorted(offsets) if offsets is not None else None
            ),
            "reachability_unavailable_reason": reason,
            "reachability_scope": "Possible offsets for contiguous diagnostic histories under independently encoded raw ten-item windows; masks and learned weights can remove influence. Source recognition is a guard, not a formal proof.",
            "exact_path_counts": None,
            "path_count_unavailable_reason": "Active nonlinear paths are not measured; structural accessibility is not learned influence",
            "causality_changed_tokens": count,
            "causality_max_abs_error": causal_error if count else None,
            "all_padding_feature_max_norm": empty_norm,
            "unreachable_control_index": unreachable,
            "unreachable_control_max_abs_error": unreachable_error,
            "unreachable_control_unavailable_reason": (
                None
                if unreachable_error is not None
                else "No applicable occupied unreachable position or no alternative item"
            ),
            "readout": "maximum nonpadding index; all-padding prefixes skipped",
        }, offsets

    @staticmethod
    def _recover_assignments(domains, groups, checker, incumbent, deadline, cap=10000):
        import time

        nodes, matching_calls, candidate_checks = 0, 0, 0
        certificate = None
        if set(groups) != set(domains) or cap < 0:
            raise ValueError("Expected one capacity group per slot and nonnegative cap")
        if any(len(set(values)) != len(values) for values in domains.values()):
            raise ValueError("Candidate domains must contain unique IDs")
        if incumbent is not None and not checker(incumbent):
            raise ValueError("Supplied greedy incumbent failed complete validation")
        solution = dict(incumbent) if incumbent is not None else None

        def bounded():
            if time.perf_counter() >= deadline:
                raise TimeoutError("category_safety_cap")

        def matching(remaining, assigned):
            nonlocal matching_calls
            matching_calls += 1
            used = {(groups[s], value) for s, value in assigned.items()}
            edges = {}
            for s in remaining:
                bounded()
                edges[s] = [
                    (groups[s], v) for v in domains[s] if (groups[s], v) not in used
                ]
            owners = {}

            def augment(slot, seen):
                bounded()
                for item in edges[slot]:
                    bounded()
                    if item in seen:
                        continue
                    seen.add(item)
                    if item not in owners or augment(owners[item], seen):
                        owners[item] = slot
                        return True
                return False

            for slot in sorted(remaining):
                augment(slot, set())
            if len(owners) == len(remaining):
                return True, None
            # Alternating reachability yields a checkable Hall deficiency.
            slots = set(remaining) - set(owners.values())
            neighbors = set()
            while True:
                bounded()
                expanded = {item for s in slots for item in edges[s]}
                reached = slots | {owners[i] for i in expanded if i in owners}
                if reached == slots:
                    neighbors = expanded
                    break
                slots = reached
            # Verify the witness directly from the frozen domains, separately
            # from the augmenting-path traversal that constructed it.
            witness_neighbors = {
                (groups[s], v)
                for s in slots
                for v in domains[s]
                if (groups[s], v) not in used
            }
            if neighbors != witness_neighbors or not len(neighbors) < len(slots):
                raise AssertionError("Invalid Hall certificate")
            return False, {
                "slots": sorted(slots),
                "scoped_neighbors": sorted(neighbors),
            }

        def search(assigned):
            nonlocal nodes, candidate_checks
            bounded()
            if nodes >= cap:
                raise TimeoutError("node_cap")
            nodes += 1
            if len(assigned) == len(domains):
                return dict(assigned) if checker(assigned) else None
            remaining = [s for s in domains if s not in assigned]
            possible, _ = matching(remaining, assigned)
            if not possible:
                return None
            used = {(groups[s], v) for s, v in assigned.items()}
            available = {
                s: [v for v in domains[s] if (groups[s], v) not in used]
                for s in remaining
            }
            slot = min(remaining, key=lambda s: (len(available[s]), s))
            for value in available[slot]:
                candidate_checks += 1
                assigned[slot] = value
                found = search(assigned)
                del assigned[slot]
                if found is not None:
                    return found
            return None

        reason = None
        proof = None
        try:
            possible, certificate = matching(list(domains), {})
            if solution is not None:
                if not possible:
                    raise AssertionError("Feasible incumbent conflicts with matching")
            elif possible:
                solution = search({})
            status = (
                "certified_feasible" if solution is not None else "certified_infeasible"
            )
            proof = (
                "independent_complete_check"
                if solution is not None
                else (
                    "scoped_Hall_deficiency"
                    if certificate is not None
                    else "exhaustive_joint_search"
                )
            )
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            reason = str(exc)
            status = "certified_feasible" if solution is not None else "unresolved"
            proof = "independent_complete_check" if solution is not None else None
        return solution, {
            "proof": proof,
            "feasibility": status,
            "optimization": "not_requested",
            "nodes": nodes,
            "matching_calls": matching_calls,
            "candidate_checks": candidate_checks,
            "certificate": certificate,
            "interruption": reason,
            "assignment": solution,
        }

    def _validate_constructor(self):
        import itertools
        import time

        cases = [
            ({0: [1, 2], 1: [1]}, {0: 0, 1: 0}, False),
            ({0: [], 1: [1]}, {0: 0, 1: 0}, False),
            ({0: [1], 1: [1]}, {0: 0, 1: 0}, False),
            ({0: [1], 1: [1]}, {0: 0, 1: 1}, False),
            ({0: [1, 2, 3], 1: [1, 2]}, {0: 0, 1: 0}, True),
            # Hall deficiency without any isolated slot.
            ({0: [1, 2], 1: [1, 2], 2: [1, 2]}, {0: 0, 1: 0, 2: 0}, False),
        ]
        for domains, groups, reject_all in cases:

            def direct(a):
                return (
                    set(a) == set(domains)
                    and not reject_all
                    and all(a[s] in domains[s] for s in domains)
                    and all(
                        groups[s] != groups[t] or a[s] != a[t]
                        for s in domains
                        for t in domains
                        if s < t
                    )
                )

            exhaustive = [
                dict(zip(domains, values))
                for values in itertools.product(*(domains[s] for s in domains))
                if direct(dict(zip(domains, values)))
            ]
            found, result = self._recover_assignments(
                domains, groups, direct, None, time.perf_counter() + 5
            )
            assert (found is not None) == bool(exhaustive)
            assert result["feasibility"] == (
                "certified_feasible" if exhaustive else "certified_infeasible"
            )
            _, stopped = self._recover_assignments(
                domains, groups, direct, None, time.perf_counter() - 1
            )
            assert stopped["feasibility"] == "unresolved"
            if exhaustive:
                kept, stopped = self._recover_assignments(
                    domains, groups, direct, exhaustive[0], time.perf_counter() - 1
                )
                assert kept == exhaustive[0]
                assert stopped["feasibility"] == "certified_feasible"
            _, limited = self._recover_assignments(
                domains, groups, direct, None, time.perf_counter() + 5, cap=0
            )
            assert limited["feasibility"] in {"unresolved", "certified_infeasible"}
            if exhaustive:
                assert limited["feasibility"] == "unresolved"
                kept, limited = self._recover_assignments(
                    domains,
                    groups,
                    direct,
                    exhaustive[0],
                    time.perf_counter() + 5,
                    cap=0,
                )
                assert kept == exhaustive[0]
                assert limited["feasibility"] == "certified_feasible"
        # A covering matching can still violate a cross-plan joint predicate.
        domains, groups = {0: [1, 2], 1: [1, 2]}, {0: 0, 1: 1}

        def joint(a):
            return (
                set(a) == {0, 1}
                and all(a[s] in domains[s] for s in domains)
                and a[0] < a[1]
            )

        exhaustive = [{0: a, 1: b} for a in domains[0] for b in domains[1] if a < b]
        found, result = self._recover_assignments(
            domains, groups, joint, None, time.perf_counter() + 5
        )
        assert found in exhaustive
        assert result["feasibility"] == "certified_feasible"
        return True

    @staticmethod
    def _aggregate(rows, bootstrap=400, seed=42):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        result = {}
        for variant in sorted({r["variant"] for r in rows}):
            selected = [r for r in rows if r["variant"] == variant]
            users = sorted({r["user"] for r in selected})
            entry = {
                "users": len(users),
                "prefixes": len({(r["user"], r["cut"]) for r in selected}),
                "observations": len(selected),
            }
            for metric in (
                "delta_rank",
                "delta_hr10",
                "delta_sampled_margin",
                "delta_target_score",
                "top10_overlap",
            ):
                user_values, user_mc_variances = [], []
                for user in users:
                    records = [
                        r
                        for r in selected
                        if r["user"] == user and r.get(metric) is not None
                    ]
                    cuts = sorted({r["cut"] for r in records})
                    groups = [
                        np.asarray(
                            [r[metric] for r in records if r["cut"] == cut], dtype=float
                        )
                        for cut in cuts
                    ]
                    if not groups:
                        continue
                    user_values.append(float(np.mean([g.mean() for g in groups])))
                    # Conditional corruption variability only; missing draws cannot
                    # establish MC precision, and are never assigned zero variance.
                    user_mc_variances.append(
                        sum(float(g.var(ddof=1) / len(g)) for g in groups)
                        / len(groups) ** 2
                        if all(len(g) >= 2 for g in groups)
                        else None
                    )
                values = np.asarray(user_values)
                interval = None
                if len(values) >= 2:
                    draws = values[
                        rng.integers(0, len(values), size=(bootstrap, len(values)))
                    ].mean(axis=1)
                    interval = np.quantile(draws, [0.025, 0.975]).tolist()
                mc = None
                if user_mc_variances and all(v is not None for v in user_mc_variances):
                    mc = float(np.sqrt(sum(user_mc_variances)) / len(user_mc_variances))
                entry[metric] = {
                    "mean": float(values.mean()) if len(values) else None,
                    "ci95": interval,
                    "corruption_mc_se": mc,
                    "observed_users": len(values),
                }
            result[variant] = entry
        return result

    def _run_protocol(self, train_loader, protocol, started):
        import time

        rng = random.Random(protocol["seed"])
        self._validate_rank()
        constructor_check = self._validate_constructor()
        deadline = started + protocol["category_safety_seconds"]
        source = self.user_train.get("History", self.user_train)
        if not isinstance(source, dict):
            raise ValueError("Expected ModelView training histories")
        itemnum = int(self.network.itemnum)
        coverage, histories = Counter(), {}
        for user in sorted(source, key=str):
            try:
                history = [int(i) for i in source[user]]
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                coverage["invalid_history_users"] += 1
                continue
            if not history or any(i < 1 or i > itemnum for i in history):
                coverage["empty_or_out_of_catalog_users"] += 1
                continue
            key = str(user)
            if key in histories:
                raise ValueError("Training user IDs collide after string normalization")
            histories[key] = history
        frequency = Counter(i for h in histories.values() for i in h)
        transitions = Counter(
            (a, b) for h in histories.values() for a, b in zip(h, h[1:])
        )
        outgoing, incoming = {}, {}
        for a, b in transitions:
            outgoing.setdefault(a, set()).add(b)
            incoming.setdefault(b, set()).add(a)

        def bin_count(count):
            return (
                -1
                if count == 0
                else int(np.searchsorted([1, 4, 15], count, side="left"))
            )

        buckets = {}
        for item in sorted(frequency):
            buckets.setdefault(bin_count(frequency[item]), set()).add(item)
        users = sorted(
            u
            for u, h in histories.items()
            if len(h) > protocol["minimum_prefix_length"]
        )
        coverage["eligible_users"] = len(users)
        coverage["short_users"] = len(histories) - len(users)
        users = sorted(rng.sample(users, min(len(users), protocol["max_users"])))
        coverage["selected_users"] = len(users)
        prefix_rng = random.Random(protocol["seed"])
        cuts_by_user = {}
        for user in users:
            cuts = range(protocol["minimum_prefix_length"], len(histories[user]))
            cuts_by_user[user] = sorted(
                prefix_rng.sample(cuts, min(len(cuts), protocol["prefixes_per_user"]))
            )
        rows, baselines, failures, controls = [], [], [], []
        assignment_records = {
            (u, cut, dose, draw): {
                "user": u,
                "cut": cut,
                "dose": dose,
                "draw": draw,
                "feasibility": "unresolved",
                "optimization": "not_requested",
                "reason": "not_started",
                "selector": None,
            }
            for u in users
            for cut in cuts_by_user[u]
            for dose in protocol["doses"]
            for draw in range(protocol["draws"])
        }
        architecture, reachable = None, None

        def effects(clean, altered):
            return {
                "delta_rank": altered["rank"] - clean["rank"],
                "delta_hr10": altered["hr10"] - clean["hr10"],
                "delta_target_score": altered["score"] - clean["score"],
                "delta_sampled_margin": (
                    altered["margin"] - clean["margin"]
                    if altered["margin"] is not None and clean["margin"] is not None
                    else None
                ),
                "top10_overlap": len(set(clean["top10"]) & set(altered["top10"]))
                / len(clean["top10"]),
            }

        for user in users:
            history = histories[user]
            for cut in cuts_by_user[user]:
                if time.perf_counter() >= deadline:
                    coverage["category_safety_cap_hits"] += 1
                    continue
                coverage["sampled_prefixes"] += 1
                full_prefix, target = history[:cut], history[cut]
                prefix = full_prefix[-protocol["history_window"] :]
                if not prefix:
                    coverage["all_padding_prefixes"] += 1
                    continue
                if len(prefix) < protocol["minimum_prefix_length"]:
                    coverage["short_window_prefixes"] += 1
                    continue
                if architecture is None:
                    architecture, reachable = self._architecture(prefix)
                excluded = set(full_prefix) - {target}
                ids = np.asarray(
                    [i for i in range(1, itemnum + 1) if i not in excluded],
                    dtype=np.int64,
                )
                negatives = [int(i) for i in ids if i != target]
                if not negatives:
                    coverage["no_eligible_negatives"] += 1
                    continue
                sampled = rng.sample(
                    negatives, min(len(negatives), protocol["sampled_margin_negatives"])
                )
                clean_scores = self._catalog_scores(
                    prefix, ids, protocol["catalog_chunk_size"]
                )
                clean = self._result(ids, clean_scores, target, sampled)
                identity_scores = self._catalog_scores(
                    list(prefix), ids, protocol["catalog_chunk_size"]
                )
                identity = self._result(ids, identity_scores, target, sampled)
                controls.append(
                    {
                        "user": user,
                        "cut": cut,
                        "identity_score_max_abs_error": float(
                            np.max(np.abs(clean_scores - identity_scores))
                        ),
                        "identity_delta_rank": identity["rank"] - clean["rank"],
                    }
                )
                strata = {
                    "prefix_length": (
                        "5-15"
                        if len(prefix) <= 15
                        else "16-63" if len(prefix) <= 63 else ">=64"
                    ),
                    "target_popularity": str(bin_count(frequency[target])),
                    "repeated_target": str(target in full_prefix),
                    "transition_frequency": str(
                        bin_count(transitions[(prefix[-1], target)])
                    ),
                }
                common = {"user": user, "cut": cut, **strata}
                baselines.append({**common, **clean})
                n = len(prefix)

                def reach(index):
                    return None if reachable is None else n - 1 - index in reachable

                forbidden = set(full_prefix) | {target, 0}
                random_pools = {
                    key: sorted(bucket - forbidden) for key, bucket in buckets.items()
                }

                def candidate_pool(index, plausible):
                    key = bin_count(frequency[prefix[index]])
                    if not plausible:
                        return random_pools.get(key, [])
                    # Intersect sparse neighborhoods before copying frequency buckets.
                    following = prefix[index + 1]
                    pool = incoming.get(following, set()) & buckets.get(key, set())
                    pool -= forbidden
                    if plausible:
                        if index:
                            pool &= outgoing.get(prefix[index - 1], set())
                        pool = {
                            i
                            for i in pool
                            if bin_count(transitions[(i, following)])
                            == bin_count(transitions[(prefix[index], following)])
                            and (
                                index == 0
                                or bin_count(transitions[(prefix[index - 1], i)])
                                == bin_count(
                                    transitions[(prefix[index - 1], prefix[index])]
                                )
                            )
                        }
                    return sorted(pool)

                pools = {
                    (i, kind): candidate_pool(i, kind == "local_plausible")
                    for i in range(n - 1)
                    for kind in protocol["replacement_types"]
                }
                pairs = [
                    (r, o)
                    for r in range(n - 1)
                    for o in range(n - 1)
                    if 1 <= n - 1 - r <= 4
                    and n - 1 - o >= 5
                    and bin_count(frequency[prefix[r]])
                    == bin_count(frequency[prefix[o]])
                    and reach(r) == reach(o)
                ]
                for dose in protocol["doses"]:
                    for draw in range(protocol["draws"]):
                        audit = assignment_records[user, cut, dose, draw]

                            audit["reason"] = "category_safety_cap"

                        selected, occupied = [], set()
                        for pair in shuffled_pairs:

                                any(abs(i - j) <= 1 for i in pair for j in occupied)
                                or abs(pair[0] - pair[1]) <= 1
                            ):

                            occupied.update(pair)
                            if len(selected) == dose:

                        tag = {**common, "dose": dose, "draw": draw}
                        if len(selected) != dose:
                            audit["reason"] = "frozen_positions_not_constructed"
                            coverage["position_matching_failures"] += 1
                            failures.append(
                                {
                                    **tag,
                                    "reason": "Greedy position assignment failed; feasibility not established",

                            )
                            continue
                        plans, pool_sizes = [], []

                                indices = [p[band_index] for p in selected]

                                for index in indices:

                                    ]
                                    pool_sizes.append(

                                            "band": band,
                                            "index": index,
                                            "available": len(pool),

                            for b, band in enumerate(("recent", "older"))
                        ]

                            (p, j, index)
                            for p, (_, _, indices) in enumerate(specs)
                            for j, index in enumerate(indices)
                        ]

                            s: tuple(pools[index, specs[p][0]])
                            for s, (p, j, index) in enumerate(slots)
                        }
                        groups = {s: p for s, (p, j, index) in enumerate(slots)}

                            if set(assignment) != set(domains):
                                return False

                            if len(set(all_positions)) != 2 * dose or any(
                                abs(a - b) <= 1
                                for a in all_positions
                                for b in all_positions
                                if a != b
                            ):
                                return False
                            for p, (kind, band, indices) in enumerate(specs):

                                values = [
                                    assignment[s] for s in domains if groups[s] == p
                                ]
                                if len(set(values)) != dose:
                                    return False
                                for s, (plan, j, index) in enumerate(slots):
                                    if plan != p:
                                        continue
                                    value = assignment[s]
                                    if value not in domains[s] or value in forbidden:
                                        return False
                                    if bin_count(frequency[value]) != bin_count(
                                        frequency[prefix[index]]
                                    ):
                                        return False
                                    changed[index] = value
                                if changed[-1] != prefix[-1] or len(changed) != n:
                                    return False
                                if kind == "local_plausible":
                                    for index in indices:
                                        for a, b in (
                                            (index - 1, index),
                                            (index, index + 1),
                                        ):
                                            if a >= 0 and (
                                                transitions[changed[a], changed[b]] <= 0
                                                or bin_count(
                                                    transitions[changed[a], changed[b]]
                                                )
                                                != bin_count(
                                                    transitions[prefix[a], prefix[b]]
                                                )
                                            ):
                                                return False
                            return True

                            }
